 Posted in News

 by 
 Rogelio V. Solis , Amy Schafer , Ahmer A. Khan and Heather Harrison

 Tatum Davis, 3, helps his mother Jerrica Davis with her voting at this Jackson, Miss., precinct, Tuesday, Nov. 3, 2026. Among the limited issues considered by voters included a tourism tax for Hinds County, voting for a Hinds County District Attorney, and a U.S. Senator. MFP Photo by Rogelio V. Solis 
 Mississippians went to the polls on Tuesday, Nov. 3, to vote for four U.S. House seats, a U.S. Senate seat and a number of local and county races. Some candidates experienced success while others had to come to terms with defeat. 
 As of Thursday, Mississippi is still waiting—and will continue to wait—for the U.S. Senate race between incumbent Republican Cindy Hyde-Smith and challenging Democrat Scott Colom. 
 Here are some photos from Election Day, including voters, parties and candidate reactions.
 Voters wait in line at the precinct Olive Branch Seventh Day Adventist Church in Olive Branch, Miss., on Nov. 3, 2024. MFP Photo by Ahmer A. Khan 
 Poll worker Lisa Stewart explains the voting process to a morning voter at this Jackson, Miss., precinct on Tuesday, Nov. 3, 2026. MFP Photo by Rogelio V. Solis

 A supporter of Democratic U.S. Senate candidate Scott Colom attends his watch party at the Ice House in Jackson, Miss., on Nov. 3, 2026. MFP Photo by Heather Harrison 
 Democratic U.S. Senate candidate Scott Colom joined supporters at a watch party at the Ice House in Jackson, Miss., on Nov. 3, 2026. MFP Photo by Heather Harrison 
 U.S. Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith speaks to supporters at her victory party in Flowood, Miss., Tuesday, Nov. 3, 2026. MFP Photo by Rogelio V. Solis 
 U.S. Rep. Michael Guest, R-Miss., speaks about his reelection with reporters at U.S. Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith, R-Miss., election night reception in Flowood, Miss., Tuesday, Nov. 3, 2026. MFP Photo by Rogelio V. Solis 
 Mississippi Rep. Jeffrey Hulum III, D-Gulfport, speaks to supporters at his watch party in Gulfport, Miss., on Nov. 3, 2026. MFP Photo by Amy Schafer 
 People gathered at a watch party for Democratic U.S. House candidate Cliff Johnson at Big Bad Breakfast in Oxford, Miss., on Nov. 3, 2026. MFP Photo by Ahmer A. Khan 
 A line of people wait to vote on Election Day at Grace Baptist Church in Ocean Springs, Miss., on Nov. 3, 2026. MFP Photo by Amy Schafer 
 Democratic U.S. Senate candidate Scott Colom poses with supporters at a watch party at the Ice House in Jackson, Miss., on Nov. 3, 2026. MFP Photo by Heather Harrison 
 U.S. Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith, R-Miss., addresses supporters at her victory party in Flowood, Miss., Tuesday, Nov. 3, 2026. MFP Photo/Rogelio V. Solis 
 Early morning voters at this Jackson, Miss., precinct, feed their paper ballots into voting machines Tuesday, Nov. 3, 2026. Among the issues voters in Hinds County considered include a tourism tax for Hinds County, voting for a Hinds County District Attorney, and a U.S. Senator. MFP Photo Rogelio V. Solis

 Rogelio V. Solis is Mississippi Free Press' new senior photojournalist. A veteran journalist, Solis most recently served 28 years as the staff photographer with the Jackson bureau of The Associated Press.
 More by Rogelio V. Solis 
 Amy Schafer Mississippi Gulf Coast Bureau Reporter 
 Amy@mississippifreepress.org 
 Amy Schafer is the Mississippi Free Press' Gulf Coast bureau reporter in partnership with Report for America. A 2026 graduate of Pennsylvania State University's Schreyer Honors College, she holds degrees in advertising/public relations, global and international studies with a concentration in human rights and women's, gender and sexuality studies. Before joining MFP, she served as editor-in-chief of Penn State's student newspaper The Daily Collegian and freelanced for The Washington Post.
 More by Amy Schafer 
 Ahmer A. Khan North Mississippi Bureau Reporter 
 ahmer@mississippifreepress.org 
 North Mississippi Bureau Reporter Ahmer A. Khan is a graduate of University of Mississippi. He is bringing his combined legal and journalism training directly to communities within the bureau during a critical election cycle.
 More by Ahmer A. Khan 
 Heather Harrison State Reporter 
 heather@mississippifreepress.org 
 bluesky 
 State Reporter Heather Harrison has won more than a dozen awards for her multi-media journalism work. At Mississippi State University, she studied public relations and broadcast journalism, earning her Communication degree in 2023. For three years, Heather worked at The Reflector student newspaper: first as a staff reporter, then as the news editor and finally, as the editor-in-chief. This is where her passion for politics and government reporting began.
Heather started working at the Mississippi Free Press three days after graduation in 2023. She also worked part time for Starkville Daily News after college covering the Board of Aldermen meetings.
In her free time, Heather likes to sit on the porch, read books and listen to Taylor Swift. A native of Hazlehurst, she now lives in Brandon with her wife and their Boston Terrier, Finley, and calico cat, Ravioli.
